Subject: Post-call recap & exec summary: HelixPharma / Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick executive-friendly recap from our discovery so your execs and procurement can get aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary (business outcomes):
- Goal: Reduce clinical support triage time by 45% and reduce per-case handling cost by ~30% through automated triage and summarization powered by LLMs.
- Success metrics: 45% faster triage time, 25-30% reduction in manual FTE hours for initial review, pilot NPS target +15.

Pain points identified:
- High latency in triage; average first-response > 6 hours on certain queues.
- Manual QA and summarization is time-consuming and error-prone.
- APAC data residency / compliance considerations for some datasets.

Risks / concerns:
- SOC 2 evidence and a short compliance intake window on procurement side.
- Integration complexity with your legacy message bus (we'll need network allowlist and a staging VPN).
- Executive sponsor clarity: we heard Product (Sarah) and Clinical Ops (Tom) — procurement and legal will own contract path.

Procurement path & timeline (as discussed):
- Sarah to introduce procurement contact (Anika) this week — procurement kick-off target week of Mar 1.
- Target pilot start: Apr 4 (6-week pilot to validate triage latency and accuracy).
- Proposal: Redwood pilot package (6 weeks, 25k evaluation credit + optional waived setup fee pending Exec approval).

Next steps (action owners):
- Laura: Share Mutual Action Plan + pricing deck + SOC 2 summary (attached). (Today)
- Sarah: Introduce procurement / legal contact and confirm procurement timeline. (This week)
- Aditya: Technical deep-dive & pilot success criteria doc. (By Wed, Feb 24)
- Marissa: Coordinate executive briefing and contract team for pilot terms. (By Feb 26)

Attachments: Helix_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx, Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf, pilot_success_criteria.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Laura — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our notes. A few clarifications/follow-ups: 

1) Procurement/contact: copying Anika Patel (anika.patel@helixpharma.com) who owns SOWs and SOC/compliance intake. Anika — we are planning a pilot and will need SOC 2 Type II and a short security intake (less than 5 business days ideally).

2) Timeline: The procurement team prefers Mar 8-12 for an initial procurement sync. Can you / your team do Mar 10 at 10am PT for a 30-45 min call?

3) Pricing: The high-level pilot package you mentioned sounds good. Can you share the exact pilot pricing and any standard contract/TSAs for pilots? Also please include the escalation path (SLA exceptions, uptime expectations) since we have clinical availability concerns.

4) Data residency: Some APAC records may need to remain in-region. We'll flag specific datasets later. For now, please include any options for regional deployments in the pilot doc.

Thanks — Sarah

Sarah / Team — appreciate the clear ask. A few technical notes and commitments from our side: 

- SOC2: attaching a short SOC 2 summary (Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf). We can provide the full report under an NDA; SOC 2 Type II audit period covers 2026.
- Regional deployment options: Redwood can run a VPC-private deployment in APAC regions or use data routing to restrict certain payloads to APAC. We'll document options in the pilot playbook.
- Pilot success criteria (high-level):
  * Average triage latency reduced to <= 2 hours for targeted queue
  * Automated summarization accuracy (F1) >= 0.78 on holdout set
  * 80% of triage items routed correctly to the right SME bucket

- Integration checklist: we will need network allowlist (static egress IPs), sample dataset (anonymized), and a staging endpoint. Proposed timeline: technical kickoff week of Mar 15.
